chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinanī, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who forgot to pray the two cycles at the Standing Place of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) during the circumambulation of Hajj and Umrah.
He said: If he was in the city, he should pray two cycles at the Standing Place of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), he should pray two cycles.
For indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'And take for yourselves a place of Prayer by the standing-place of Ibrahim.'
And if he had already travelled, then I would not order him to return.

key_terms.الرَّكْعَتَانِ: The two cycles of prayer performed after Tawaf.
key_terms.بِالْبَلَدِ: In the city (Mecca), indicating the pilgrim has not yet left the holy precincts.
key_terms.طَوَافُ الْحَجِّ: The circumambulation of the Kaaba performed during Hajj.
key_terms.طَوَافُ الْعُمْرَةِ: The circumambulation of the Kaaba performed during Umrah.
key_terms.مَقَامُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ: The Standing Place of Ibrahim (AS), a stone in the Masjid al-Haram where Prophet Ibrahim stood while building the Kaaba.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim forgets to pray at Maqam Ibrahim during Tawaf?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the ruling for a pilgrim who forgets the two rak'ahs of prayer at Maqam Ibrahim, distinguishing between those still in Mecca, who must return to fulfill this Quranic command, and those who have departed, who are exempt from returning. This ruling highlights the practical application of the verse 'Take the Maqam of Ibrahim as a place of prayer,' emphasizing that the obligation is tied to physical presence rather than an absolute requirement for every pilgrim regardless of location. The hadith reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on ease and avoiding undue hardship (rukhas) when the specific condition of being in the city is no longer met.
